hits.draft_en:
Underrated craft fair hack: ask the vendor at the next table which show was their best this year, and why.

Ten minutes of setup chatter tells you more about a market than any event listing.

What's the most useful thing a booth neighbor ever told you?
hits.video_tip: Phone at a booth during setup, 10-15s: one line to camera with the hack, then a cut to two neighboring tables being set up. Captions on, no music needed.

hits.name: Codie Sanchez
hits.hook: Make goals if you want to win one time.
hits.text:
Make goals if you want to win one time.
Use systems if you want to win every time.
hits.draft_en:
Set a sales goal if you want one good show.
Build a system if you want a good season.

For market vendors the system is boring on purpose:
- the same packing list, every night before a show
- every item priced before it leaves the house
- a tally of what sold, written down before teardown
- rebook shows by profit per hour, not by how busy it felt

Vendors: what's one piece of your system that took a full season to figure out?
hits.video_tip: Talking-head, 20-30s: say the two opening lines to camera, then show the four system steps as quick on-screen text over hands packing a bin. End on the question as a caption.

hits.name: Codie Sanchez
hits.hook: Words to turn to when it’s hard… https://t.co/tH6y9TQ52T
hits.text: Words to turn to when it’s hard… https://t.co/tH6y9TQ52T
hits.draft_en:
Things to remember on a slow market day:

- One slow show isn't the whole season.
- Foot traffic isn't buyers. Note who stopped and what they picked up.
- Someone who took your card can still buy next week.
- Slow hours are for restocking the front row and fixing price signs.
- Judge the show by profit at the end, not by how the afternoon felt.

Save this for the next quiet Saturday. What gets you through a slow show?
hits.video_tip: Pair with a 1080x1080 cream-paper sketch card of the five lines (house style, one burnt-orange accent) instead of video; if filming, a 15s slow pan across an empty aisle with each line as a caption.
